public_rationale: Part 1 holds. He hedged it ('does not appear'). Challenger's year-end tally shows employers named AI for only 4,247 of 721,677 announced US job cuts in 2023, about 0.6%. So AI did not appear to be replacing a large number of workers. Part 2 has evidence on both sides. The best-known 2023 case went badly: NEDA replaced its helpline staff with a chatbot and pulled it within days after it gave harmful advice. But the most prominent case at the time of the post was Klarna. In February 2024 Klarna said its AI did the work of 700 agents, with customer satisfaction on par with humans. Ed himself cites Klarna in the same paragraph as the one company that improved its bottom line. Klarna's figures are self-reported, but they are a documented case that was not reported as terrible at the time. So the first clause is supported and the general claim about results is only partly supported.
limitations: 'Pretty terrible' and 'a large number' have no stated measure, so the grade depends on interpretation.

our_interpretation: The claim has two parts. Part 1 is hedged ('does not appear to be'). It holds if the best public data at the time showed AI being cited for only a small share of job cuts. It does not require proof that no displacement was happening.
Part 2 is firm. It holds if the known cases where firms replaced workers with AI before the post went badly. It fails if a prominent known case was reported, at the time, as going well.
Target period: from the start of 2023, the first full year of the generative AI boom he is discussing, to the post date. This is my reading of a present-tense claim made without a named period.
criteria.support_condition: Part 1: labour data from 2023 to early 2024 show AI cited for only a small share of announced job cuts. Part 2: the documented replacements of workers with AI in that period had poor results.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Part 1: data show AI was cited for a large share of job cuts by early 2024. Part 2: a prominent documented replacement in the period was reported as working as well as or better than humans.
